source_excerpt: In accordance with international consensus regarding the core set of outcome measures for phase III clinical trials in OA (Smith 2019), each RCT was required to include assessment of at least one of the following. 1.Knee pain severity 2.Self-reported physical function 3.Quality of life Time points We assessed clinical outcomes (pain, physical function, quality of life) at three time points: immediately at the end of the treatment (post-treatment), up to 12 months after cessation of the intervention, and more than 12 months after cessation of the intervention. Each included study was required to report measurement of outcomes for at least one of these time periods. In contrast to the previous review, we did not assess outcomes at 2 to 6 months after treatment because of the volume of research we anticipated finding, as well as our interest in longer-term outcomes.

outcome_text_raw: Adverse effects (as defined by the authors of the included trials). We planned to assess this as both the number of participants with at least one adverse event, as well as individual adverse events. Unlike some other diets that might eliminate essential foods or have adverse side effects, the DASH diet does not appear to have any known reported adverse effects. However, adverse events can be related to food allergens and intolerance. We planned to report this depending on the availability of data from trials. The unit for the number of participants with at least one adverse event is the count (number of cases). For individual adverse events, units depend on the specific adverse event (e.g. counts, percentages). The reporting of adverse events related to food allergens and intolerance would follow similar units based on the available data from trials

outcome_text_raw: Global state 2.1 Relapse In case more measures of relapse were reported, we gave priority to: (i) relapse defined with operationalised criteria (e.g. worsening on a symptom scale); (ii) clinical judgement. 2.2 Recovery Recovery is intended as "the ability to function in the community, socially and vocationally, as well as being relatively free of disease- related psychopathology" (Andreasen 2005). We extracted the number of participants in recovery, based on this definition or on similar definitions provided in the studies. 2.3 Remission Symptomatic remission according to Andreasen criteria (Andreasen 2005). 2.4 Clinically important change in global state (e.g. global impression of much improved, or more than 50% improvement on a rating scale such as Clinical Global Impression (CGI)) 2.5 Average endpoint or change score on a global state scale
